success.title: Adoption Success Stories
success.lead: Real families. Real quirks. Really happy endings. Meet a few of our alumni who found their forever homes—and solved a small, funny problem along the way.

story_1.title: The Couch Potato Turned Jogging Buddy
story_1.meta: Adopted by Ana & Leo • 6 months ago
story_1.body: Bella arrived with champion-level napping skills and a strong preference for sofas over sidewalks. One day she spotted a squirrel, sprinted a full block, and discovered she actually loves running. Now she leads every morning jog (and still guards the couch on rest days).
story_1.solved: “She won’t walk!” turned into “She outruns us!”—thanks to a structured routine and a squirrel-shaped motivation.

story_2.title: The Curtain Climber
story_2.meta: Adopted by the Rivera family • 3 months ago
story_2.body: Whiskers is a world-class acrobat… which the living room curtains discovered first. After a few daring ascents, her family set up a floor-to-ceiling cat tree by the window. She still surveys her kingdom from the top—curtains unfrayed, dignity intact.
story_2.solved: Redirected climbing energy with a tall cat tree, window perch, and daily play sessions.

story_3.title: The Great Chewer
story_3.meta: Adopted by Sam, Maya & kids • 8 months ago
story_3.body: Thumper adored his new home—and the tasty, spaghetti-like “snacks” running along the baseboards. The family bunny-proofed with cord covers and offered willow sticks and hay cubes. Thumper now channels his talents into designated chew time.
story_3.solved: Cable covers + chew toy rotation = zero surprise phone-charger casualties.

story_4.title: The Guard Dog with a Soft Spot
story_4.body: Max took home security very seriously—maybe too seriously for delivery drivers. Then he met the neighbor’s toddler, who shared tiny biscuits through the fence. Now Max differentiates between “protect the house” and “cookie o’clock” like a pro.
story_4.solved: Calm-greeting training at the door and planned cookie meet-and-greets with friendly faces.

story_5.title: The Microwave Impersonator
story_5.meta: Adopted by the Nguyen family • 4 months ago
story_5.body: Matilda learned to perfectly mimic the microwave’s final beep. Chaos ensued; snacks were checked, dinners re-checked, and laughter levels soared. The family moved the perch away from the kitchen and taught a new “all done!” cue instead.
story_5.solved: New cue training + strategic perch placement = fewer false alarms, more party tricks.

story_6.title: The Music Critic
story_6.meta: Adopted by Priya & Arun • 2 months ago
story_6.body: Luna loved her new home—except band practice night. The family introduced a cozy den in a quiet room and paired it with treat-filled lick mats during rehearsals. Now she “reviews” the performances from her nook with a satisfied tail thump.
story_6.solved: Noise sensitivity eased with a safe space, enrichment, and gradual sound desensitization.
